main_body: Snow-laden conifer (fir tree): tiered dark green canopy with snow bands on each tier, short brown trunk at the bottom
top_band: none as a single top surface; stacked snow bands (white/pale blue, ~2-4 rows each) lie on branch tiers, e.g. rows 13-15, 23-26, 34-37, 45-49, forming a conifer silhouette rather than one top over a front face
evidence: Organic conifer: each branch tier has a snow layer on top with dark green foliage hanging below it and a darker underside shadow, which reads as a lit upper surface plus a front mass. The layered tiers give volume and the trunk is visible at the base. There is no flat panel elevation and no receding side face. The tree reads as a normal 3/4 map tree, and the organic kind fits. It is not a rigid top and front box, but the snow caps on each tier act as top bands with shaded foliage below.

style.evidence: The candidate has a dark green outline that leans toward the foliage tone rather than near-black. Foliage uses about 4 greens, from deep teal-black through mid green to a lighter highlight on the left, and snow adds white, pale blue and grey-blue steps. Clumpy foliage edges and snow drips give some texture. It has fewer leaf clumps and less per-tile variation than the Beodeul broadleaf references, and the lower tiers include fairly smooth dark green patches. It is slightly less rich than the references but has no large flat fills, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.
